chunks: Ten - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated, saying: Ubays ibn Hisham narrated, from Abdullah ibn Jubala, from Ahmad ibn al-Harith, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Indeed, the master of this matter has a disappearance, in which he will say:
So I fled from you when I feared you, then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me of the messengers.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Command (referring to the Imam/Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What Quranic verse will the Mahdi recite during his occultation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) identifies the verse 'So I fled from you, and my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers' (Quran 19:28) as the specific recitation of the Mahdi during his occultation. This selection underscores the theological concept of the Imam as the ultimate inheritor of prophetic wisdom, linking his hidden leadership directly to the divine authority and the continuity of the prophetic mission. In Shia eschatology, this verse serves as a key identifier for the Mahdi, affirming his status not merely as a ruler but as a divinely appointed guide possessing the same spiritual stature as the prophets.
